claims.text: Al0.5NbTa0.8Ti1.5V0.2Zr is a refractory high-entropy alloy whose ductility can be altered through phase-morphology control.
Al0.5NbTa0.8Ti1.5V0.2Zr can be processed to exhibit a complete ductile–brittle–ductile transition.
A continuous ordered B2 matrix in this alloy is associated with brittle behavior.
A continuous disordered BCC matrix with discrete B2 precipitates provides greater room-temperature ductility than a continuous B2 matrix.
A continuous disordered BCC matrix produces ductility at elevated temperatures.
The as-cast/HIPed alloy has a continuous ordered B2 matrix and is brittle.
Solutionizing followed by annealing at approximately 600 °C for an extended duration can invert the microstructure to a continuous disordered BCC matrix with discrete B2 precipitates.
The relevant mechanical behavior can be evaluated by room-temperature and 600 °C uniaxial testing under a controlled strain rate.
The continuity and distribution of ordered B2 relative to disordered BCC is the structural mediator of ductility.
Temperature-induced ordering transitions govern the alloy's ductility.
At intermediate temperatures, ordering kinetics favor formation of a continuous B2 phase.
The continuous B2 phase suppresses dislocation mobility and thereby causes embrittlement.
The embrittlement caused by continuous B2 is analogous to temper embrittlement in conventional alloys.
At lower and higher temperatures, or after appropriate heat treatment, the matrix becomes disordered BCC and supports dislocation motion.
The continuous-B2 condition has high yield strength but low room-temperature fracture strain.
The transition occurs within a narrow temperature or processing window.
Changes in alloy composition or heat-treatment schedule may prevent formation or inversion of the continuous brittle phase.
A complete ductile–brittle–ductile transition has not been comprehensively demonstrated in this alloy system.

contradictions.description: The initial/as-cast-HIPed state is defined as a brittle continuous-B2 matrix, but the predicted outcome also describes the alloy as ductile when 'initially processed' with a BCC matrix, without distinguishing a different initial processing condition.

The intervention states that prolonged annealing near 600 °C produces a continuous disordered BCC matrix with discrete B2 precipitates, whereas the mechanism states that intermediate temperatures favor formation of a continuous brittle B2 phase.
